summary: Clemente Merlo was an Italian linguist who studied at the University of Pavia (c. 1899–1903). He held a post at the University of Pisa from circa 1909 to 1954.
Clinton B. Seely is an Indologist who held posts at the University of Chicago, attested in 2007, and in 2026 as Professor, Emeritus of South Asian Languages and Civilizations.

Clyde Kluckhohn studied at Princeton, Wisconsin-Madison, Oxford, Vienna, and Harvard. He held posts at the University of New Mexico (c. 1932–1934) and Harvard University (c. 1935–1960), and taught McKim Marriott.

Colette Caillat was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Louis Renou, Jules Bloch, and Walther Schubring. She held posts at the CNRS, University of Lyon, Sorbonne University, Collège de France, and Institut de France.

Colette Sciberras is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David Edward Cooper and Simon P. James, and also studied under traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who completed his studies under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria.
Colin Mackenzie was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He studied at Dollar Academy and served as Surveyor General at the Survey of India from 1810 to 1815.
Colin Turnbull was a scholar in religious studies who studied at Westminster School (c. 1936–1942), Magdalen College (c. 1942–1949), and Banaras Hindu University (c. 1949–1951).

Collett Cox is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her PhD at Columbia under Alex Wayman and Yoshito S. Hakeda, studied at Tokyo and Ryukoku, and held posts at the University of Washington.
Conor Roddy is a philosopher who studied under Arindam Chakrabarti and Roger T. Ames, completing a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2011).
Conrad Bursian was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Leipzig and Berlin. He held posts at Leipzig, Zurich, Tübingen, Jena, and Munich, and taught Albert Grünwedel.

Conrad M. Arensberg was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Harvard University (c. 1931–1934). He held a post at Columbia University from circa 1946 to 1979 and taught Morton Klass.

Constance Kassor is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She earned a BA at Smith College and a PhD at Emory University under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, later joining Smith College's faculty.
Constance Powell Chin is a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. She studied under Christian Luczanits and earned a master's degree from San Jose State University in 2012.

Constantin Regamey was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and linguist. He studied at Warsaw and Paris under Schayer, Przyluski, Lalou, and Turczyński, and held posts at Warsaw, Lausanne, Fribourg, and the Swiss Asia Society.

Corinna May Lhoir works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Attested in 2026, she studied at Ghent University and the University of Hamburg, also serving at Hamburg as a lecturer and program coordinator in yoga studies.

Cornelis Jan Kuiken is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Groningen in 2002 under doctoral supervisors Timothy H. Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer, having also studied under Jaap den Hollander.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele was a religious studies scholar and historian who studied at the Remonstrant Seminary and University of Amsterdam. He held posts at the Remonstrant Seminary, Leiden University, and the University of Edinburgh.

Corrado Pensa is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Raniero Gnoli. He served as Professor of Religions and Philosophy of India and the Far East at Sapienza University of Rome.
Cortland Dahl is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and was mentored by Sarah Harding, Anne Helm, and Erik Pema Kunsang.
